eras.name: Creation and the first families
eras.summary: The world made and called good, the first people placed in it, and the first fracture — disobedience, exile from the garden, and a brother's murder.

eras.name: The Flood
eras.summary: A world grown violent, one righteous family preserved through it, and a covenant never to unmake the earth by water again.

eras.name: The Patriarchs
eras.summary: Four generations — Abraham, Isaac, Jacob, Joseph — through whom God begins to build a nation out of one childless couple's promise.

eras.name: The Exodus
eras.summary: Israel is enslaved in Egypt, delivered through the plagues and the Red Sea, receives the law at Sinai, and spends forty years in the wilderness before arriving at the plains of Moab, ready to cross into the promised land.
eras.approxRange: roughly 40 years, from slavery in Egypt to the plains of Moab

eras.name: The Judges
eras.summary: Centuries after the Exodus, a chaotic period where everyone did what was right in their own eyes. Ruth's is a quiet story of loyalty inside it -- and it ends by naming David's great-grandparents.
eras.approxRange: centuries after the Exodus, before Israel's kings

stories.title: The world is made
stories.summary: God speaks the heavens and the earth into being, fills them, makes humanity in his own image, and calls all of it very good.

stories.title: The garden
stories.summary: God forms the man from dust, breathes life into him, plants a garden for him to tend, and makes the woman so he is not alone.

stories.title: The fall
stories.summary: The serpent persuades the woman that God is holding out on her. She eats, gives to her husband, and the two of them are put out of the garden.

stories.title: Cain and Abel
stories.summary: God accepts Abel's offering and not Cain's. Warned that sin is crouching at his door, Cain kills his brother in the field anyway.

stories.title: The flood
stories.summary: In a violent generation Noah is found righteous. He builds the ark exactly as commanded, rides out the flood, and comes out to a rainbow and a promise.

stories.title: The call of Abram
stories.summary: God tells a seventy-five-year-old man to leave his country, his relatives and his father's house for a land he will only be shown once he goes. He goes.

stories.title: Abram and Lot part ways
stories.summary: Their herds outgrow the land. Abram, the elder, gives his nephew first choice; Lot takes the well-watered Jordan valley and settles toward Sodom.

stories.title: The covenant of the pieces
stories.summary: God promises Abram offspring as countless as the stars. Abram believes him, and it is credited to him as righteousness.

stories.title: Hagar and Ishmael
stories.summary: Tired of waiting, Sarai gives her servant Hagar to Abram. Hagar conceives, is mistreated, and flees — and meets the God who sees her.

stories.title: A new name, a new sign
stories.summary: God appears to ninety-nine-year-old Abram, renames him Abraham — father of many nations — and gives circumcision as the sign of an everlasting covenant.

stories.title: Three visitors and Sarah's laugh
stories.summary: Three strangers accept Abraham's hospitality and promise Sarah a son within the year. Sarah, listening at the tent door, laughs.

stories.title: Abraham pleads for Sodom
stories.summary: Abraham bargains with God for the city — down from fifty righteous to ten — appealing to the Judge of all the earth to do right.

stories.title: Isaac is born
stories.summary: At a hundred years old Abraham holds the son he was promised a quarter-century earlier. They name him Isaac — laughter.

stories.title: Hagar sent away
stories.summary: Sarah demands Hagar and Ishmael be sent off. Their water runs out in the wilderness; God hears the boy crying and opens Hagar's eyes to a well.

stories.title: The binding of Isaac
stories.summary: God asks Abraham for the son he waited a lifetime for. Abraham goes, knife raised — and God provides a ram caught in the thicket instead.

stories.title: Sarah is buried
stories.summary: Sarah dies at a hundred and twenty-seven. Abraham mourns her, then buys the cave of Machpelah — the first piece of the promised land he ever owns.

stories.title: Rebekah at the well
stories.summary: Abraham's servant asks God for a sign and Rebekah gives it — watering ten camels for a stranger. She agrees to go, and becomes Isaac's wife.

stories.title: Twins at war in the womb
stories.summary: Rebekah is barren twenty years, then carries twins who struggle inside her. Esau is born first; Jacob follows, gripping his heel.

stories.title: A birthright for a bowl of stew
stories.summary: Esau comes in from the field starving and trades his birthright as firstborn to Jacob for a meal.

stories.title: The stolen blessing
stories.summary: Rebekah dresses Jacob in Esau's clothes and goatskins. Blind Isaac blesses the wrong son, and Jacob has to run for his life.

stories.title: The ladder at Bethel
stories.summary: Fleeing with nothing but a staff, Jacob sleeps on a stone and dreams of a stairway to heaven. God stands above it and promises to keep him wherever he goes.

stories.title: Seven years for Rachel
stories.summary: Jacob the deceiver is deceived: he works seven years for Rachel and is given Leah instead, then works seven more. Leah bears sons; Rachel does not.

stories.title: Wrestling until daybreak
stories.summary: Alone at the Jabbok the night before facing Esau, Jacob wrestles a man until dawn, refuses to let go without a blessing, and limps away renamed Israel.

stories.title: Esau runs to meet him
stories.summary: Jacob braces for the brother he cheated, sending gifts ahead. Esau runs to him, embraces him, and weeps.

stories.title: Joseph's dreams
stories.summary: Jacob's favourite son tells his brothers he dreamed they would bow to him. They already hated him; now they cannot speak a kind word to him.

stories.title: Sold by his brothers
stories.summary: They see him coming and plot to kill him, throw him in a pit instead, and sell him to passing traders for twenty pieces of silver.

stories.title: Potiphar's house and prison
stories.summary: Yahweh is with Joseph and he prospers, until he refuses his master's wife and is thrown into prison for it.

stories.title: Dreams in prison and palace
stories.summary: Joseph interprets a cupbearer's and a baker's dreams, is forgotten for two years, then reads Pharaoh's dream of famine and is made second in Egypt.

stories.title: "I am Joseph"
stories.summary: After testing the brothers who sold him, Joseph sends everyone out and weeps aloud: God sent him ahead of them to preserve life.

stories.title: Jacob comes to Egypt
stories.summary: Told his son is alive, Jacob goes down to Egypt to see him, and the family settles in Goshen through the famine.

stories.title: Jacob blesses his sons
stories.summary: Dying, Jacob gathers his twelve sons and speaks over each one what they will become — the shape of the tribes of Israel.

stories.title: "You meant evil; God meant it for good"
stories.summary: With their father dead, the brothers fear revenge. Joseph weeps and tells them what he has understood all along about the God who redirected their evil.

stories.title: Hidden, then found
stories.summary: To save her infant son from Pharaoh's death decree, Jochebed hides him three months, then sets him afloat in a basket on the Nile - where Pharaoh's own daughter finds and raises him.

stories.title: Moses flees to Midian
stories.summary: After killing an Egyptian who was beating a Hebrew, Moses flees for his life, settles in Midian, defends a priest's daughters at a well, and marries one of them.

stories.title: The burning bush
stories.summary: Keeping his father-in-law's flock at Horeb, Moses sees a bush that burns without being consumed. God calls him by name, reveals his own name, and sends him back to Egypt to deliver Israel - over every objection Moses raises.

stories.title: Aaron meets him in the wilderness
stories.summary: Moses takes his wife and sons and returns to Egypt. Aaron goes out to meet him at God's mountain and kisses him; together they gather Israel's elders, and the people believe and bow down to worship.

stories.title: "Let my people go"
stories.summary: Moses and Aaron confront Pharaoh again and again with the same demand. Each time he refuses, a plague strikes Egypt; each time it lifts, his heart hardens again.

stories.title: The Passover
stories.summary: On the night of the tenth plague, Israel is told to mark their doorposts with blood so death will pass over them. That night Egypt's firstborn die, and Pharaoh finally lets Israel go.

stories.title: Crossing the Red Sea
stories.summary: With Pharaoh's army closing in and the sea ahead, Moses tells the people to stand still. The sea divides, Israel crosses on dry ground, and the pursuing army is destroyed.

stories.title: The song of the sea
stories.summary: On the far shore, Moses sings of what Yahweh has done. Miriam takes up a tambourine, and all the women dance and sing after her.

stories.title: Bread from heaven, water from the rock
stories.summary: In the wilderness the people run out of food, then water. God answers both times — bread appearing with the dew each morning, water from a struck rock.

stories.title: The battle with Amalek
stories.summary: Joshua leads Israel's fighting men against Amalek while Moses holds up his hands on a hilltop. When his hands grow heavy, Aaron and another man hold them up until sunset, and Joshua wins.

stories.title: The covenant at Sinai
stories.summary: At the mountain, God offers Israel a covenant — his own possession, a kingdom of priests — and gives the commandments, beginning with no other gods and honoring father and mother.

stories.title: The golden calf
stories.summary: While Moses is on the mountain, the people grow impatient and ask Aaron to make them a god. Moses comes down, breaks the tablets in anger, and then goes back up to beg God to forgive them rather than destroy them. Joshua, meanwhile, has not left the tent.

stories.title: "Merciful and gracious"
stories.summary: God gives Moses new tablets and passes before him, proclaiming his own character: merciful, gracious, slow to anger, abundant in loving kindness — and still just.

stories.title: The glory fills the tabernacle
stories.summary: The tabernacle is finished exactly as instructed. A cloud covers it, and Yahweh's glory fills it so completely that even Moses cannot enter.

stories.title: Aaron ordained as priest
stories.summary: After seven days of ordination rites, Aaron and his sons offer the first sacrifices as priests. Fire comes out from before Yahweh and consumes the offering, and the whole camp shouts and falls on its face.

stories.title: Nadab and Abihu
stories.summary: Two of Aaron's sons offer incense with fire God never authorized, and fire from Yahweh kills them on the spot, in front of their father. Moses tells Aaron this is exactly what God meant by being shown holy among those who come near him. Aaron says nothing.

stories.title: The blasphemer
stories.summary: A man in the camp curses Yahweh's name during a fight. Israel holds him in custody until Yahweh tells Moses exactly what to do: everyone who heard him lays a hand on his head, and the whole community stones him.

stories.title: Miriam and Aaron oppose Moses
stories.summary: Miriam and Aaron speak against Moses over his Cushite wife, and challenge whether Yahweh speaks only through him. Miriam is struck with leprosy; Moses immediately begs God to heal her, and she is shut outside the camp seven days.

stories.title: The twelve spies
stories.summary: Twelve men scout Canaan. Ten report giants and fortified cities and spread fear; Caleb and Joshua insist God will give them the land. The people side with the fearful report and refuse to go up, so God condemns that whole generation to wander forty years and die in the wilderness — only Caleb and Joshua will enter.

stories.title: Korah's rebellion
stories.summary: Korah and his followers accuse Moses and Aaron of taking too much power for themselves. Moses says the ground itself will show who Yahweh sent — and the earth opens and swallows Korah, his household, and everything he owns.

stories.title: Water from the rock, again
stories.summary: Nearly forty years after the first time, the people again have no water. This time God tells Moses to speak to the rock — but Moses, furious, strikes it twice instead. The water still comes, but Moses and Aaron are told neither of them will enter the promised land because of it.

stories.title: Miriam and Aaron die
stories.summary: Miriam dies at Kadesh. Later that year, Moses strips Aaron of his priestly garments on Mount Hor and puts them on his son Eleazar; Aaron dies there, and all Israel mourns him thirty days.

stories.title: The bronze serpent
stories.summary: The people complain again about the journey, and Yahweh sends venomous snakes among them. When they confess and ask Moses to intercede, God tells him to make a bronze snake and put it on a pole — anyone who is bitten and looks at it lives.

stories.title: Balaam's donkey
stories.summary: Hired by a foreign king to curse Israel, the prophet Balaam is stopped on the road by his own donkey, who sees the angel of Yahweh blocking the way and speaks in protest. Balaam's eyes are opened too — and when the moment comes, he blesses Israel instead of cursing them, seeing a king who will rise from Jacob far in the future.

stories.title: Moses commissions Joshua
stories.summary: In front of all Israel, Moses tells Joshua to be strong and courageous — he will lead the people into the land Yahweh swore to their fathers. Moses lays his hands on him, and Joshua is filled with the spirit of wisdom.

stories.title: Moses views the land, and dies
stories.summary: From Mount Nebo, Yahweh shows Moses the whole land he swore to Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob — and tells him he will not cross over into it himself. Moses dies there at a hundred twenty, his eye undimmed and his strength unspent, and no prophet like him has risen in Israel since.

stories.title: Famine drives them to Moab
stories.summary: A famine sends Elimelech, Naomi, and their two sons from Bethlehem to Moab. The sons marry Moabite women, Ruth and Orpah. Then all three men die, leaving Naomi with her daughters-in-law and nothing else.

stories.title: "Where you go, I will go"
stories.summary: Naomi urges her daughters-in-law to go home to Moab and remarry. Orpah, weeping, does. Ruth refuses to leave, binding herself to Naomi's people and Naomi's God. They arrive in Bethlehem with nothing, at the start of the barley harvest.

stories.title: Ruth gleans in Boaz's field
stories.summary: Ruth goes out to gather leftover grain to feed herself and Naomi, and happens into the field of Boaz, a relative of Naomi's dead husband. He has noticed everything she has done for Naomi, and tells his workers to leave extra for her on purpose.

stories.title: Ruth asks for redemption
stories.summary: Naomi sends Ruth to Boaz at the threshing floor at night to ask him, as a near kinsman, to spread his garment over her — a claim of protection and marriage, not scandal. Boaz agrees, but names a closer relative who has first right to redeem her.

stories.title: Boaz redeems Ruth
stories.summary: At the town gate, the nearer kinsman declines to redeem Elimelech's field once he learns it comes with Ruth. Boaz redeems it himself and marries her. She bears a son, Obed — the grandfather of Jesse, the father of David.

lifeEvents.title: Sent by God to meet Moses
lifeEvents.description: Yahweh tells Aaron to go into the wilderness to meet his brother.

lifeEvents.title: Becomes Moses' spokesman
lifeEvents.description: God tells Moses that Aaron, who can speak well, will be his mouth.

lifeEvents.title: Speaks for Moses before Pharaoh
lifeEvents.description: He repeats Yahweh's demand to Pharaoh through the escalating plagues.

lifeEvents.title: Keeps the first Passover
lifeEvents.description: He and Moses lead Israel through the night of the tenth plague.

lifeEvents.title: Holds up Moses' hands
lifeEvents.description: When Moses' arms grow heavy on the hilltop, Aaron holds one side up until Joshua wins the battle.

lifeEvents.title: Makes the golden calf
lifeEvents.description: Pressured by the people, he collects their gold and fashions it into an idol.

lifeEvents.title: Ordained as priest
lifeEvents.description: He and his sons offer the first sacrifices; fire from Yahweh consumes the offering and the camp shouts.

lifeEvents.title: Loses Nadab and Abihu
lifeEvents.description: Fire from Yahweh kills both sons in front of him for an offering he never commanded. Aaron says nothing.

lifeEvents.title: Sees Miriam struck with leprosy
lifeEvents.description: He and Moses watch it happen the moment the cloud lifts from the Tent.

lifeEvents.title: Stands with Moses against Korah
lifeEvents.description: Korah accuses them both of taking too much power.

lifeEvents.title: Barred from the promised land
lifeEvents.description: He shares in the consequence of Moses striking the rock instead of speaking to it.

lifeEvents.title: Dies on Mount Hor
lifeEvents.description: His garments pass to Eleazar; all Israel mourns him thirty days.

lifeEvents.title: Brings the firstborn of his flock
lifeEvents.description: A keeper of sheep, he brings the fat portions of the firstborn, and God accepts it.

lifeEvents.title: Killed in the field
lifeEvents.description: His brother kills him, and his blood cries out from the ground.

lifeEvents.title: Ordained a priest
lifeEvents.description: He is set apart alongside his father and brothers.

lifeEvents.title: Dies offering unauthorized fire
lifeEvents.description: He and his brother Nadab offer incense God never commanded, and are killed instantly.

lifeEvents.title: Called out of Haran
lifeEvents.description: Told to leave his country, his relatives and his father's house for a land he will be shown.

lifeEvents.title: Gives Lot first choice of the land
lifeEvents.description: The elder yields to the younger to keep peace between their herdsmen.

lifeEvents.title: Counts the stars, and believes
lifeEvents.description: Promised offspring beyond counting, he believes God, and it is credited to him as righteousness.

lifeEvents.title: Takes Hagar, and Ishmael is born
lifeEvents.description: Ten years into waiting, Sarai's plan produces a son who is not the promised one.

lifeEvents.title: Renamed Abraham
lifeEvents.description: God renames him father of many nations and gives circumcision as the covenant sign.

lifeEvents.title: Bargains with God for Sodom
lifeEvents.description: Dust and ashes, he presses God down from fifty righteous to ten.

lifeEvents.title: Isaac is born
lifeEvents.description: The promise arrives twenty-five years after it was made.

lifeEvents.title: Sends Hagar and Ishmael away
lifeEvents.description: Distressed, he does it at Sarah's insistence and God's word — and God provides for them.

lifeEvents.title: Offers Isaac on Moriah
lifeEvents.description: He raises the knife over the son he waited a lifetime for, and God provides the ram.

lifeEvents.title: Buries Sarah at Machpelah
lifeEvents.description: He mourns her, then buys the cave — the first ground in the promised land he owns.

lifeEvents.title: Sends for a wife for Isaac
lifeEvents.description: He sends his servant back to his own people, and the servant is led to Rebekah.

lifeEvents.title: Dies at a hundred and seventy-five
lifeEvents.description: Isaac and Ishmael bury him beside Sarah.

lifeEvents.title: Formed from the dust
lifeEvents.description: Yahweh God shapes the man from the ground and breathes life into him.

lifeEvents.title: Names the animals, and is given Eve
lifeEvents.description: No suitable helper is found among the creatures, so God makes the woman.

lifeEvents.title: Eats the fruit
lifeEvents.description: Eve gives him some of the fruit and he eats it too.

lifeEvents.title: Put out of the garden
lifeEvents.description: Sent out to work ground that now resists him, with cherubim barring the way back.

lifeEvents.title: Hired to curse Israel
lifeEvents.description: A Moabite king pays him to curse the people camped at his border.

lifeEvents.title: His donkey speaks
lifeEvents.description: She sees the angel of Yahweh blocking the road before he does, and asks him what she's done to deserve being struck.

lifeEvents.title: Blesses Israel instead of cursing them
lifeEvents.description: Every time he opens his mouth to curse, blessing comes out — including a glimpse of a king far in Israel's future.

lifeEvents.title: Notices Ruth gleaning
lifeEvents.description: He has already heard what she did for Naomi, and tells his workers to leave extra grain for her on purpose.

lifeEvents.title: Praises her loyalty
lifeEvents.description: "May Yahweh repay your work... under whose wings you have come to take refuge."

lifeEvents.title: Agrees to redeem her, if the nearer kinsman won't
lifeEvents.description: He tells her to stay until morning, and names the one relative with a prior claim.

lifeEvents.title: Redeems the field and Ruth at the gate
lifeEvents.description: The nearer kinsman declines; Boaz redeems Elimelech's inheritance and takes Ruth as his wife.

lifeEvents.title: Fathers Obed
lifeEvents.description: His son with Ruth becomes the grandfather of Jesse, the father of David.

lifeEvents.title: His offering is not accepted
lifeEvents.description: He brings fruit of the ground; God has no regard for it, and Cain's face falls.

lifeEvents.title: Warned that sin crouches at the door
lifeEvents.description: God tells him sin's desire is for him, but he is to rule over it.

lifeEvents.title: Kills his brother
lifeEvents.description: He speaks to Abel in the field, and there he murders him.

lifeEvents.title: Marked and sent east
lifeEvents.description: Made a wanderer, but given a mark so no one who finds him will kill him.

lifeEvents.title: Spies out Canaan
lifeEvents.description: He silences the people's fear: "Let's go up at once, and possess it; for we are well able."

lifeEvents.title: Promised he will enter the land
lifeEvents.description: "Because he had another spirit with him, and has followed me fully" — he and Joshua alone of their generation will enter Canaan.

lifeEvents.title: Becomes high priest
lifeEvents.description: Moses puts Aaron's garments on him on Mount Hor, the same day Aaron dies.

lifeEvents.title: Leads his family to Moab
lifeEvents.description: He takes his wife and two sons from Bethlehem to Moab to escape a famine.

lifeEvents.title: Dies in Moab
lifeEvents.description: He never sees his family return to Bethlehem.

lifeEvents.title: Born first, red and hairy
lifeEvents.description: The firstborn twin, with his brother gripping his heel.

lifeEvents.title: Sells his birthright
lifeEvents.description: Famished from the field, he trades it for bread and lentil stew, and despises it.

lifeEvents.title: Finds the blessing gone
lifeEvents.description: He cries out with a great and bitter cry, and plans to kill his brother.

lifeEvents.title: Runs to embrace Jacob
lifeEvents.description: Twenty years later he meets his brother with four hundred men — and falls on his neck weeping.

lifeEvents.title: Made from the man's side
lifeEvents.description: God makes the woman so the man will not be alone.

lifeEvents.title: Deceived by the serpent
lifeEvents.description: Persuaded the fruit will make her wise, she takes it and eats.

lifeEvents.title: Called the mother of all living
lifeEvents.description: Adam names her Eve, because she is the mother of all the living.

lifeEvents.title: Bears Cain, then Abel
lifeEvents.description: She bears two sons, and lives to see one kill the other.

lifeEvents.title: Flees into the wilderness
lifeEvents.description: Mistreated after she conceives, she runs — and is found by an angel at a spring.

lifeEvents.title: Names God "the God who sees me"
lifeEvents.description: The only person in Genesis to give God a name.

lifeEvents.title: Shown a well in the desert
lifeEvents.description: Out of water and unable to watch her son die, she weeps — and God opens her eyes.

lifeEvents.title: Born to Abraham and Sarah
lifeEvents.description: The promised son, born when his father was a hundred.

lifeEvents.title: Carries the wood up Moriah
lifeEvents.description: He asks where the lamb is, and is told God will provide one.

lifeEvents.title: Marries Rebekah
lifeEvents.description: He brings her into his mother's tent, and is comforted after Sarah's death.

lifeEvents.title: Twins born after twenty years
lifeEvents.description: He prays for his barren wife, and Esau and Jacob are born.

lifeEvents.title: God appears to him at Beersheba
lifeEvents.description: "Don't be afraid, for I am with you" — the promise made to his father, repeated to him.

lifeEvents.title: Blesses the wrong son
lifeEvents.description: Blind and old, he gives Esau's blessing to Jacob, and trembles violently when he realises.

lifeEvents.title: Born to Hagar
lifeEvents.description: Abram's firstborn, named before birth: God hears.

lifeEvents.title: Sent away with his mother
lifeEvents.description: God hears the boy where he is and promises to make him a great nation.

lifeEvents.title: Buries his father with Isaac
lifeEvents.description: The two sons stand together at Abraham's grave.

lifeEvents.title: Born holding Esau's heel
lifeEvents.description: The second twin, named for the grip he came out with.

lifeEvents.title: Buys the birthright
lifeEvents.description: He trades a bowl of stew for his brother's rights as firstborn.

lifeEvents.title: Steals his father's blessing
lifeEvents.description: Disguised in his brother's clothes, he lies to his blind father's face.

lifeEvents.title: Dreams of the ladder at Bethel
lifeEvents.description: Running for his life, he is met with a promise: I am with you wherever you go.

lifeEvents.title: Works fourteen years for Rachel
lifeEvents.description: Deceived into marrying Leah first, he serves seven more years for the woman he loves.

lifeEvents.title: Wrestles until daybreak
lifeEvents.description: He refuses to let go without a blessing, and walks away limping and renamed Israel.

lifeEvents.title: Meets Esau again
lifeEvents.description: Braced for revenge, he is embraced instead.

lifeEvents.title: Believes Joseph is dead
lifeEvents.description: Shown the bloodied coat, he refuses to be comforted.

lifeEvents.title: Goes down to Egypt
lifeEvents.description: Told his son is alive and ruling Egypt, he goes to see him before he dies.

lifeEvents.title: Blesses his twelve sons
lifeEvents.description: He tells each of them what they will become, and dies.

lifeEvents.title: Hides her son three months
lifeEvents.description: Seeing he is a fine child, she conceals him from Pharaoh's decree as long as she can.

lifeEvents.title: Sets him afloat in a basket
lifeEvents.description: She coats a papyrus basket with tar and pitch and lays it among the reeds by the riverbank.

lifeEvents.title: Hired to nurse her own son
lifeEvents.description: Pharaoh's daughter unknowingly pays Moses' own mother to nurse him.

lifeEvents.title: Dreams that his brothers bow
lifeEvents.description: The favourite son tells them, and they hate him all the more.

lifeEvents.title: Thrown in a pit and sold
lifeEvents.description: His brothers strip him, pit him, and sell him to traders for twenty pieces of silver.

lifeEvents.title: Prospers in Potiphar's house
lifeEvents.description: Yahweh is with him, and everything he does succeeds.

lifeEvents.title: Refuses Potiphar's wife
lifeEvents.description: "How then can I do this great wickedness, and sin against God?" — and he is imprisoned for it.

lifeEvents.title: Forgotten in prison for two years
lifeEvents.description: He interprets the cupbearer's dream and asks to be remembered. He isn't.

lifeEvents.title: Reads Pharaoh's dream
lifeEvents.description: Seven years of plenty, seven of famine — and a plan to survive them.

lifeEvents.title: Made second in Egypt
lifeEvents.description: Pharaoh sets him over the whole land, with the signet ring off his own hand.

lifeEvents.title: Reveals himself to his brothers
lifeEvents.description: He weeps so loudly the Egyptians hear it: I am Joseph. Is my father still alive?

lifeEvents.title: Sees his father again
lifeEvents.description: He falls on Jacob's neck in Goshen and weeps a long time.

lifeEvents.title: Forgives his brothers outright
lifeEvents.description: "You meant evil against me, but God meant it for good, to save many people alive."

lifeEvents.title: Defeats Amalek
lifeEvents.description: He leads Israel's fighting men while Moses' upheld hands decide the battle.

lifeEvents.title: Won't leave the Tent of Meeting
lifeEvents.description: After Moses speaks with God face to face and leaves the tent, his young aide stays behind.

lifeEvents.title: Spies out Canaan
lifeEvents.description: One of the twelve, and one of only two who came back believing Israel could take the land.

lifeEvents.title: Commissioned by Moses
lifeEvents.description: Moses lays hands on him before all Israel; he is filled with the spirit of wisdom.

lifeEvents.title: Leads a rebellion against Moses and Aaron
lifeEvents.description: He gathers two hundred fifty leaders and accuses them of taking too much on themselves.

lifeEvents.title: Swallowed by the earth
lifeEvents.description: The ground opens beneath him, his household, and everything he owns.

lifeEvents.title: Given to Jacob in Rachel's place
lifeEvents.description: Veiled and substituted by her father, she wakes married to a man who wanted her sister.

lifeEvents.title: Bears son after son
lifeEvents.description: Seeing she is unloved, God opens her womb; she names her sons for her longing to be loved.

lifeEvents.title: Names her fourth son Judah
lifeEvents.description: "This time I will praise Yahweh" — the line the kings will come from.

lifeEvents.title: Chooses the Jordan valley
lifeEvents.description: Given first pick, he takes the well-watered plain and pitches his tent toward Sodom.

lifeEvents.title: Rescued by Abram
lifeEvents.description: Captured when the kings sack Sodom, he is brought back by his uncle's night raid.

lifeEvents.title: Pulled out of Sodom
lifeEvents.description: The angels seize his hand and lead him out; his wife looks back.

lifeEvents.title: Watches over the basket
lifeEvents.description: She stands at a distance to see what will happen to her brother.

lifeEvents.title: Arranges for their mother to nurse him
lifeEvents.description: She steps forward and offers to find a Hebrew nurse for the child - their own mother.

lifeEvents.title: Leads the women in song
lifeEvents.description: She takes a tambourine and leads the women in singing and dancing after the sea closes over Egypt's army.

lifeEvents.title: Speaks against Moses
lifeEvents.description: She and Aaron challenge Moses over his marriage and his unique standing before God.

lifeEvents.title: Struck with leprosy
lifeEvents.description: She is shut outside the camp seven days after Moses prays for her.

lifeEvents.title: Dies at Kadesh
lifeEvents.description: The text records her death and burial in a single sentence.

lifeEvents.title: Hidden three months, then set adrift
lifeEvents.description: His mother hides him as long as she can, then sets him afloat on the Nile in a coated basket.

lifeEvents.title: Found and adopted by Pharaoh's daughter
lifeEvents.description: She recognises him as a Hebrew child, has compassion on him, and raises him as her own son.

lifeEvents.title: Kills an Egyptian, and flees
lifeEvents.description: Grown and aware of his people's suffering, he kills an Egyptian beating a Hebrew, and flees when it becomes known.

lifeEvents.title: Meets Zipporah at a well
lifeEvents.description: He defends a priest's seven daughters from shepherds driving them off, and is given one of them in marriage.

lifeEvents.title: Sees the burning bush
lifeEvents.description: A bush burns and is not consumed. God calls his name twice; he answers, Here I am.

lifeEvents.title: Called and sent to confront Pharaoh
lifeEvents.description: Told to bring Israel out of Egypt, he objects four times - who am I, what is your name, what if they don't believe, I am slow of speech - and is answered every time.

lifeEvents.title: Returns to Egypt
lifeEvents.description: He takes his wife and sons, puts them on a donkey, and sets out with God's staff in his hand.

lifeEvents.title: Reunited with Aaron
lifeEvents.description: Aaron meets him at God's mountain and kisses him; together they persuade Israel's elders.

lifeEvents.title: Confronts Pharaoh again and again
lifeEvents.description: He and Aaron repeat the same demand through nine plagues, and Pharaoh's heart hardens every time.

lifeEvents.title: Institutes the Passover
lifeEvents.description: He tells Israel to mark their doors with blood on the night of the tenth plague.

lifeEvents.title: Leads Israel through the sea
lifeEvents.description: He stretches out his hand and the sea divides; Israel crosses on dry ground.

lifeEvents.title: Sings on the far shore
lifeEvents.description: "Yah is my strength and song. He has become my salvation."

lifeEvents.title: Brings bread and water from nothing
lifeEvents.description: He relays God's provision of manna and strikes the rock at Horeb for water.

lifeEvents.title: Receives the covenant and the commandments
lifeEvents.description: God offers Israel a covenant through him, and gives the Ten Commandments.

lifeEvents.title: Breaks the tablets, then intercedes
lifeEvents.description: Furious at the golden calf, he shatters the tablets — then goes back up the mountain and offers to be blotted out himself rather than let the people be destroyed.

lifeEvents.title: Hears God proclaim his own character
lifeEvents.description: "Merciful and gracious, slow to anger, and abundant in loving kindness and truth."

lifeEvents.title: Can't enter his own tent
lifeEvents.description: God's glory fills the finished tabernacle so completely that even Moses is kept out.

lifeEvents.title: Ordains Aaron and his sons
lifeEvents.description: He carries out seven days of ordination rites exactly as commanded.

lifeEvents.title: Rules on the blasphemer
lifeEvents.description: He holds the man until Yahweh tells him exactly what the community must do.

lifeEvents.title: Prays for Miriam's healing
lifeEvents.description: The instant she is struck with leprosy, he cries out, "Heal her, God, I beg you!"

lifeEvents.title: Sends twelve spies into Canaan
lifeEvents.description: Ten come back afraid; only Caleb and Joshua say Israel can take the land.

lifeEvents.title: Confronts Korah's rebellion
lifeEvents.description: He tells the assembly the ground itself will show who Yahweh sent.

lifeEvents.title: Strikes the rock in anger
lifeEvents.description: Told to speak to the rock, he strikes it twice instead — and is barred from entering the promised land for it.

lifeEvents.title: Buries Aaron on Mount Hor
lifeEvents.description: He strips Aaron of his priestly garments and puts them on Eleazar before Aaron dies.

lifeEvents.title: Makes the bronze serpent
lifeEvents.description: Anyone bitten by the venomous snakes who looks at it lives.

lifeEvents.title: Commissions Joshua as his successor
lifeEvents.description: He lays his hands on Joshua in front of all Israel and tells him to be strong and courageous.

lifeEvents.title: Views the promised land from Mount Nebo
lifeEvents.description: Yahweh shows him all of it, and tells him he will not cross over.

lifeEvents.title: Dies in the land of Moab
lifeEvents.description: At a hundred twenty years old, his eye not dim nor his strength gone. No prophet like him has arisen in Israel since.

lifeEvents.title: Ordained a priest
lifeEvents.description: He is set apart alongside his father and brothers.

lifeEvents.title: Dies offering unauthorized fire
lifeEvents.description: He and his brother Abihu offer incense God never commanded, and are killed instantly.

lifeEvents.title: Leaves Bethlehem for Moab
lifeEvents.description: Famine drives her, her husband, and their two sons to Moabite country.

lifeEvents.title: Loses her husband and both sons
lifeEvents.description: Elimelech dies, then ten years later both her sons — leaving her with only her two daughters-in-law.

lifeEvents.title: Urges Ruth and Orpah to go home
lifeEvents.description: With nothing left to offer them, she tells her daughters-in-law to return to their mothers' houses and remarry.

lifeEvents.title: Returns to Bethlehem, calling herself Mara
lifeEvents.description: "I went out full, and Yahweh has brought me home again empty."

lifeEvents.title: Sends Ruth to Boaz's field, then to the threshing floor
lifeEvents.description: She recognises Boaz as a near kinsman and coaches Ruth on how to ask him for redemption.

lifeEvents.title: Nurses her grandson Obed
lifeEvents.description: The women of Bethlehem tell her a son has been born to her, and name him Obed.

lifeEvents.title: Found righteous in a violent generation
lifeEvents.description: Noah walks with God while the earth is filled with violence.

lifeEvents.title: Builds the ark
lifeEvents.description: He does all that God commanded him — exactly.

lifeEvents.title: Rides out the flood
lifeEvents.description: Shut in by God, the family and the animals survive while the waters cover the earth.

lifeEvents.title: Given the rainbow
lifeEvents.description: God sets his bow in the cloud as the sign of a covenant with every living creature.

lifeEvents.title: Marries into Naomi's family, then is widowed
lifeEvents.description: She marries one of Naomi's sons and is left a widow with Ruth and Naomi.

lifeEvents.title: Returns to her own people
lifeEvents.description: She weeps and kisses Naomi goodbye, and goes back to Moab — a choice the text never condemns.

lifeEvents.title: Refuses, plague after plague
lifeEvents.description: Each time a plague lifts, his heart hardens and he refuses to let Israel go.

lifeEvents.title: Finally lets Israel go
lifeEvents.description: After his own son dies in the tenth plague, he tells Moses and Aaron to take Israel and leave.

lifeEvents.title: Pursues Israel to the sea
lifeEvents.description: He changes his mind and chases Israel with his army, which the sea then destroys.

lifeEvents.title: Finds the basket in the reeds
lifeEvents.description: Bathing at the river, she sees the basket, sends a servant for it, and hears the baby crying.

lifeEvents.title: Adopts him as her son
lifeEvents.description: She names him Moses - because I drew him out of the water.

lifeEvents.title: Met at the well
lifeEvents.description: Jacob rolls the stone away for her flock and weeps aloud when he kisses her.

lifeEvents.title: Barren while her sister bears sons
lifeEvents.description: Loved but childless, she envies Leah and pleads with Jacob for children.

lifeEvents.title: God remembers her
lifeEvents.description: She bears Joseph, and asks for one more son.

lifeEvents.title: Dies giving birth to Benjamin
lifeEvents.description: She names him son of my sorrow with her last breath; Jacob renames him son of my right hand.

lifeEvents.title: Waters ten camels for a stranger
lifeEvents.description: Her kindness is the sign Abraham's servant had prayed for.

lifeEvents.title: Agrees to go
lifeEvents.description: Asked whether she will leave with the man, she says simply: I will go.

lifeEvents.title: Told two nations are in her womb
lifeEvents.description: The children struggle inside her; she is told the elder will serve the younger.

lifeEvents.title: Engineers Jacob's blessing
lifeEvents.description: She overhears Isaac's plan and dresses Jacob to take his brother's blessing.

lifeEvents.title: Marries into Naomi's family, then is widowed
lifeEvents.description: She marries one of Naomi's sons; ten years later he is dead along with his father and brother.

lifeEvents.title: Refuses to leave Naomi
lifeEvents.description: "Where you go, I will go... your people will be my people, and your God my God."

lifeEvents.title: Gleans in Boaz's field
lifeEvents.description: She asks to gather leftover grain, and happens into the field of a man who already knows what she has done for Naomi.

lifeEvents.title: Asks Boaz for redemption
lifeEvents.description: At the threshing floor at night, she asks him to spread his garment over her as a near kinsman.

lifeEvents.title: Redeemed and married by Boaz
lifeEvents.description: He takes her as his wife at the town gate, before the elders of the city.

lifeEvents.title: Bears a son, Obed
lifeEvents.description: Her son becomes the grandfather of Jesse, the father of David.

lifeEvents.title: Leaves Haran with Abram
lifeEvents.description: She goes with him to a land neither of them has seen.

lifeEvents.title: Gives Hagar to Abram
lifeEvents.description: Childless and out of patience, she tries to build a family another way.

lifeEvents.title: Laughs at the tent door
lifeEvents.description: Told she will have a son within the year, she laughs — and is asked whether anything is too hard for Yahweh.

lifeEvents.title: Bears Isaac at ninety
lifeEvents.description: God has made laughter for her, and everyone who hears will laugh with her.

lifeEvents.title: Dies at Kiriath Arba
lifeEvents.description: Abraham comes to mourn for her and to weep for her.

lifeEvents.title: Met at a well in Midian
lifeEvents.description: Moses defends her and her sisters from shepherds driving them off, and waters their flock.

lifeEvents.title: Given to Moses in marriage
lifeEvents.description: Her father gives her to Moses, content that he should dwell with them.

lifeEvents.title: Bears a son, Gershom
lifeEvents.description: Moses names him Gershom - for he said, I have lived as a foreigner in a foreign land.
